properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape extended too far south (into the Irish Hill Playground green space) and not far enough east, versus the diagram's actual fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) in a crop spanning this block's 3 internal sub-division cells, merged them (morphological closing across the thin cell-divider lines), and extracted the outer contour (OpenCV) -- a clean rectangle at pixel (698,838)-(1075,957). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed zero overlap with PKS, C2, or HDY1/2. RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (same day, full geometry restart): the 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' overlap mentioned in this file's own accuracy_caveat no longer applies -- Building 2 was found to be badly mislocated (a west-side vacant lot, not its real east-cluster position next to Buildings 12 and 21) and has been relocated; it no longer overlaps this parcel at all. See that file's own digitization_method. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (found while investigating a user-flagged Irish Hill Playground misplacement): the 2026-09-16 pixel bbox above (698,838)-(1075,957) turns out to be the SAME confirmed 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug already found and fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3 that same day -- dividing each value by 1.08 (698/1.08=646.3, 838/1.08=776.9, 1075/1.08=995.4, 957/1.08=886.1) lands almost exactly on a fresh, independent color-fill extraction on page171.png at its correct 2200x1700 resolution: (647,776)-(996,887). This block was evidently never rechecked when that bug was fixed elsewhere. Re-measured via the same method (isolate RGB [128,193,219], morphological closing across the 3 internal cell dividers, OpenCV outer contour) directly on page171.png and converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. New shape is a plain rectangle, confirmed 0 overlap with PKS, HDY3, or C2 (33-39m clearance to each) and used to correct the previously-wrong Irish Hill Playground clip boundary (see that file's own digitization_method). CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'C1 now is cut by 21st street when it should just be south of it'): the fix above was itself wrong -- both it AND the pre-existing committed geometry it replaced overlapped the real, confirmed 21st St centerline (CNN 15233000) by well over 100m of its length (145.7m for the old version, 128.9m for the resolution-bug fix), i.e. this was never actually a resolution-scaling problem for this specific edge, and fixing the resolution bug alone did not fix the real issue. Root cause: this diagram-transform, even correctly applied, places this row of blocks (C1's own latitude band, roughly midway between the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors and its more-distant east side) measurably too far north relative to where the real street actually is -- PKS, immediately to this block's west and fronting the same stretch of 21st St, sits with 0 overlap against this same street segment, so the discrepancy is specific to this eastern extension of the row, not a sitewide bias. Rather than patch the transform, ground-truthed this block's own north edge directly against the real street centerline (the same one PKS already sits correctly against): computed the real centerline's latitude at each of this block's own longitudes (linear interpolation along CNN 15233000, which is nearly straight over this span) and set this block's north edge 6.8m south of it (this project's own empirically-measured real curb-to-centerline half-width -- see street_geometry.py), then shifted the two south corners by the same amount to preserve the block's shape/depth from the diagram. Confirmed 0 overlap with 21st St, Michigan St's own north-south segment (8999001), and Building 113-116's real footprint; 11.7% of this block's area now falls in the buffered real-street layer (a normal corner-lot-style sliver along Michigan St's separate north-south alignment near this block's west edge, well under this project's 15% flag threshold), down from 45%. This move also required re-clipping Irish Hill Playground, which had been clipped against this block's previous (wrong) position -- see that file's own digitization_method. RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). This restored position again overlaps the real Building 113-116 footprint (~1015 sq m) -- re-added to check_geometry_quality.py's EXPECTED_OVERLAP_PAIRS. Whether that specific overlap is itself correct is flagged for a visual check against the rendered map before treating it as settled. RECONSIDERED 2026-09-17 (same day, before treating the ~1015 sq m overlap with real Building 113-116 as expected): checked the D4D text itself (Section 1.3, Figure 1.3.3 legend) for that building's actual fate rather than assuming a demolition -- it lists Building 113-116 as one of the 'Historic Buildings to be Rehabilitated' (kept, not demolished), part of the National Register-listed UIW Historic District. That rules out the 'planned demolition, overlap is expected' reasoning already used elsewhere on this site for buildings that ARE slated for removal. Since Building 113-116's own footprint is real/surveyed (high confidence) and this block's own boundary is diagram-transform-derived (5-15m tolerance), clipped this block against the real building footprint via shapely difference() rather than accepting the overlap -- area drops from ~3,730 to ~2,701 sq m. Simplified the resulting boundary (114 raw vertices down to 14, following the building's own real corners) rather than leaving a jagged trace. REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. North edge snapped to 6.8m south of the new anchor line's centerline at each corner's own longitude (~27.4m shift at the west corner, ~30.8m at the east corner), own depth preserved. Re-checked against the real Building 113-116 footprint at this new position: 0 overlap (the previous ~1015 sq m overlap, clipped in the prior round, no longer occurs at all -- this block moved south, away from the building, so the full pure-diagram rectangle is used here rather than a clipped shape). EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: should border Louisiana St on its east side, same as PKN/PKS were extended to Michigan St): east edge (NE/SE) extended to real Louisiana St (CNN 15237000) at each corner's own latitude, offset 9.8m west (6.8m curb + ~3m sidewalk allowance, same standard used elsewhere this round). Checked against the RAW Assessor building layer first, which flagged a false positive ~1827 sq m overlap with Building 113-116 -- that raw layer still includes the piece south of the real 21st St curb that this project's own curated pier70_building_113_116.geojson already excludes (see that file and src/verify_block_fill.py's documented limitation); checked against the curated file directly and confirmed 0 overlap (a clean ~6.5m gap). Area grows from ~3,724 to ~4,815 sq m.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. RESOLVED 2026-09-16: no longer overlaps 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' -- that file's placement was corrected to its real position elsewhere on the site (see that file's digitization_method). CORRECTED 2026-09-17: this block was found to carry the same resolution-mismatch bug as PKN/PKS/HDY3 -- see digitization_method. Its true south edge sits ~26m further north than previously recorded, which had been silently eating into Irish Hill Playground's real extent. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 against the real, rehabilitated Building 113-116 footprint (not a planned-demolition overlap) -- see digitization_method.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential, 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (a uniform height, not a 65-90 ft range). One of two 100%-affordable parcels in this cluster is C1B (a sub-portion of this parcel) per a 2020 Port Commission resolution -- the other is C2A (see Parcel C2). No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
